entries.claim: Ordinary least squares chooses the intercept and slope that minimise the sum of squared residuals, and the fitted line passes through (x-bar, y-bar)
entries.notes: Fitted line identity follows from the normal equations

entries.claim: The least-squares slope equals r times s_y / s_x, so its sign matches the correlation, and the intercept is y-bar minus the slope times x-bar
entries.notes: Identical numerators for r and b1

entries.claim: R-squared equals 1 minus SSE/SST and equals the squared correlation in simple linear regression
entries.notes: Holds for models with an intercept

entries.claim: Regressions between independent integrated (random-walk) time series can report high R-squared and misleading significance, known as spurious regression
entries.notes: Motivates inspecting residual autocorrelation for trending series

entries.claim: Cook's distance measures how much the fitted coefficients change when one observation is removed, combining residual size and leverage
For x = 1..5 and y = 2,4,5,4,5 the least-squares fit is y-hat = 2.2 + 0.6x with R-squared 0.6
entries.notes: Deterministic small-sample arithmetic reproducible with numpy

entries.claim: The scatter, residual-diagnostic panels, R-squared bar and interactive slope are hand-constructed teaching figures
entries.notes: No real dataset used; values are schematic
